$comment: ONE source of truth for every constant both surfaces need.
The Python pipeline and the browser client are necessarily two
implementations, but they must not be two SPECIFICATIONS. Before this
file existed, the browser client retyped HERO_STILL_FORMATS,
VIDEO_FORMATS, the palette bands, the glow colours and the cutout
gates as JavaScript literals, and nothing would have caught them
drifting apart except someone noticing that the two surfaces produced
different output.
Both sides now READ this file:
Python  src/lotstretcher/spec.py
Browser web/public/js/spec.js
and tests/test_spec_parity.py asserts the Python modules agree with
it, so a constant changed in only one place fails the suite.
What belongs here: values both surfaces use. What does not: anything
only one can do (NVENC, SwinIR, scraping, audio), and any logic.
This is a data file, not a program.

heroStillFormats.$comment: compose/pipeline.py::HERO_STILL_FORMATS. The same three shapes as the video, at the same sizes, so a still and a clip of one shape pair up.

$comment: compose/hero_video.py. fpsBrowser differs from fps deliberately:
the CLI renders at 25 to match its audio-bar timing, and the
browser has no audio to sync to, so it uses the web-standard 30.
Stated here rather than hidden in one implementation.
compose/spin.py and core/src/spin.rs: the half-turn spin made by
cross-dissolving a vehicle's real angle cutouts. angleOrder is
geometric (front to rear) on purpose, not the carousel's reveal
order; heightFrac and groundFrac hold every anchor at one size on
one ground line so the cut reads as rotation, not a slideshow.
imaging/interior.py and core/src/interior.rs: the exposure lift and
white balance every interior photo gets, and the callout scrim.
The lift fades out between highlightKnee and highlightCeiling of
the ORIGINAL luminance so blown windows are left alone; white
balance is estimated from bright near-neutral pixels only, partial
and capped, so a tan cabin is not neutralised into grey.
imaging/sticker.py, sticker.js and core/src/sticker.rs: the Monroney
parser. placeholderMarkers identify Ford's 'check back later' PDF;
makes are looked for in the page furniture; panelSplit finds the
gutter of a two-panel landscape page (see find_panel_split_x).
imaging/wheel.py and photos.py: the wheel money shot. The models
(CLIP gates, CLIPSeg localisation, SAM2 cutout) are the host's; the
mask arithmetic they feed (core/src/mask.rs: bounds, components,
the angle gate, the crop, the duplicate check) is the core's. Every
number here was calibrated on real inventory photos; the reasoning
is in wheel.py next to each name.
Browser-side routing floors. No CLI counterpart yet: the CLI has a
richer cascade (tiebreak and wheel-detail classifiers) that the
distilled students do not reproduce, so the browser leans on
confidence where the CLI leans on a second opinion.
interiorLean: the scene model's 'detail' class holds close-ups of both kinds (the CLI files
interior close-ups under exterior/ without a cutout, so they trained as 'detail'), and a wide cabin
shot can land there at low margin; when 'detail' wins but interior scores at least this much, the
photo is treated as interior, since a shipped-and-lifted cabin shot beats a dropped one (F-150 check:
the two cabin shots called detail had interior at 0.49 and 0.37; the banner had 0.24).
server/processing.py::CUT_TYPES. 'blur' is accepted by the server
for request-shape compatibility and currently maps to 'complete',
which is a real tracked gap there. browserExposed marks what the
web client offers, so the gap is recorded in one place instead of
being rediscovered.
CLI capabilities a browser cannot do. Listed so the web client can
say WHY something is missing rather than silently omitting it.
browserUnsupported.upscale: SwinIR and Real-ESRGAN are far too heavy for a browser tab
browserUnsupported.wheels: Wheel money shots need CLIPSeg and SAM2, which have no browser build yet
browserUnsupported.nvenc: No GPU encoder access from a page
browserUnsupported.scraping: Cross-origin HTML is unreadable, and dealer sites sit behind Cloudflare challenges
browserUnsupported.inventorySync: Long-running batch work with no browser equivalent
browserUnsupported.audio: The CLI's beat-synced video needs an audio loop and ffmpeg muxing
browserUnsupported.assets: Borders and stock backgrounds need an asset library (Tier 1)
browserUnsupported.scrape: A browser cannot read another site's page. Use 'From a listing' instead: a bookmarklet run on the vehicle page hands its record and photo links to this app.

$comment: EVERY composition control, defined ONCE.
The browser renders its Options pane from this block, and
tests/test_control_parity.py asserts each control's `cli` flag
really exists in cli.py. Adding a control is therefore a single
spec edit plus the CLI flag it names: the UI picks it up with no
JavaScript change, and forgetting the CLI side fails the suite.
Fields: key (the option name both sides use), type, default,
cli (the flag it maps to), cliInvert (the flag DISABLES it, as
--no-glow does), surfaces (where it applies), requires (a host
capability it needs), unit/min/max/step for ranges.
A control may be browser-only (surfaces without 'cli'), but ONLY with a cliNote saying why. That keeps the exemption visible instead of letting 'no flag yet' quietly become permanent divergence.

`looks` are one-tap presets: a name and the control values it sets. The app's Look pane renders them as chips above the groups and --look NAME applies the same values on the CLI, with any flag given explicitly winning over the look. Every key must name a control and every value must be one that control accepts (tests/test_control_parity.py).

_: The subset of a DealerInspire vdp_gtm_payload that scrape.normalize_vehicle reads.
The app's saved-page reader keeps ONLY these keys, so a page read on the device carries what
the CLI would have used and nothing else. tests/test_listing_parity.py asserts the
list covers every key normalize_vehicle actually touches.
The on-disk layout of a listings library, as vehicle_pipeline writes it and as both
library readers (server/library.py and web/public/js/library/) read it. One vehicle is
<root>/<bucket>/<folder>/ with details.json beside a bundle/ of finished output.
tests/test_library_parity.py asserts the pipeline writes exactly these names.
What a VIN encodes by standard, with no database: the check digit (validity), the model-year letter,
and the first three characters naming the manufacturer (wmi). Model, trim and engine are encoded
per manufacturer in positions 4-8 and need NHTSA's database, so the app reads those from the listing
address's year-make-model slug instead. Decoded on the device by web/public/js/pipeline/vin.js and
lotstretcher/vin.py from these same tables; tests/test_vin_parity.py holds them to each other.
A wmi value that is a list names a manufacturer whose code spans brands; the address's slug decides, else the app asks.
